speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As part of the Government's commitment to give every child a good start and to make Singapore a great place for families, we have undertaken various efforts to raise the affordability, accessibility and quality of our early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To be effective, ECDA has to work in close partnership with the operators of around 1,800 childcare centres and kindergartens in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Such trust is possible because of committed and passionate teachers, as well as quality centres, and all this is underpinned by a sound and robust regulatory framework that upholds quality.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Regulatory standards underpin the foundation of a good quality preschool, much like the stacking ring toy that we played with when we were young, the one with the concentric circles, increasingly smaller.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We find that in pre-schools today, it is a toy that helps children to develop their fine motor skills, it comes in different colours and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The biggest ring is at the base and it forms the foundation.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Early Childhood Development Centres (ECDC) Bill seeks exactly to be that strong and reliable base for the sector − to consistently provide good quality programmes that give our young parents peace of mind when it comes to the safety, well-being and development of their children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In short, this Bill will ensure higher and more consistent quality standards across the early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Before I go into the key provisions of the Bill, I wish to thank Members of this House, the early childhood sector and the public for their support and valuable suggestions.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The proposals in the Bill were made through extensive consultations over the past two years with operators, parents, teachers, early childhood experts, industry partners and the general public.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Parents who came for ECDA's focus group discussions − I think they came to appreciate and realise the amount of effort that operators and teachers have to put in to ensure that the preschool is safe and conducive for their children's development.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA received strong support on the need to raise centre quality, and we also calibrated our proposals based on the feedback received from the different stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Members will notice that the Bill focuses on early childhood development − we emphasise holistic care and education as an integral part of our children's growth.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In this regard, childcare centres and kindergartens will be collectively regulated as "early childhood development centres" under a common licensing framework, which this harmonised Bill is better able to support, rather than being separately regulated under the Child Care Centres Act and Education Act, as they are today.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What this means is that, instead of the current "lifetime subscription" model for kindergartens, where they are registered one-off under the Education Act, all centres will now run on the "renewal subscription" model, which is already the practice for childcare centres today under the Child Care Centres Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Centres, essentially, will be approved to operate for a period of time and will be re-assessed when they renew their licence tenures.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This requires centres to consciously put in effort to maintain their standards to continue their operations for another tenure.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Key areas of focus include physical space norms and design, environment safety and hygiene, programme staff quality and, of course, staff-to-child ratios.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Better quality centres will be awarded longer licence tenures, and this will incentivise them and encourage them to perform better.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA officers will continue to conduct unannounced visits to centres periodically to ensure that centres maintain their standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The focus of this Bill is to regulate what we currently define today to be childcare centres and kindergartens.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Bill, therefore, provides for the exclusion and exemption of premises where specialised services are provided to a niche group.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It also excludes centres regulated under other legislations for distinctly different purposes, or operated by or on behalf of the Government, and hence directly accountable to this House.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Examples include enrichment centres, standalone foreign system kindergartens, kindergartens affiliated with foreign-system primary schools, or kindergartens by the Ministry of Education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Such entities are currently not under ECDA's purview and will similarly not come under this new Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As many of us can agree, people, especially teachers, are at the heart of every early childhood development centre.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Parts 3 and 4 of the Bill have provisions to enable better and more consistent quality of staff who interact with children, especially early childhood professionals, given their important role during children's formative years.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, the Bill will ensure that all principals and teachers meet the prevailing professional qualification requirements before assuming their appointments.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In addition, all persons working in centres will also need to be approved by ECDA for their suitability before they can start work at the centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This will cover, for example, principals and teachers, cooks and cleaners, as well as enrichment vendor staff.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: All individuals will be assessed on their track record, especially pertaining to children's safety.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One benefit of a common regulatory framework across the early childhood sector is a common administrative process to register staff.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This facilitates our teachers' movement between childcare centres and kindergartens, which many teachers had called for earlier.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I also believe that this regulatory framework will further enhance the professional standing and standards of our early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Nevertheless, my Ministry is very mindful of the manpower and other ground constraints faced by operators.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They have given us feedback, and we do understand them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As a regulator, ECDA will strive to ensure that its administrative processes are efficient and that its regulatory requirements are responsive to operators' needs, while ensuring sevice quality and the safety of our children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, ECDA is exploring allowing non-teaching staff, such as cooks and cleaners, to support trained teachers in supervising outdoor play time.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The constant dialogue that we have with the sector must continue, so that the feedback can come back to us and this allows us to calibrate these proposals.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As with any enterprise, good governance and management are critical success factors for early childhood development centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The new Bill will further prohibit recalcitrant operators, whose licences had been revoked, from operating centres under another proxy.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This allows ECDA to prevent such persons from continuing to misdirect centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA will also penalise licensees for knowingly allowing such unsuitable persons from managing their centre's business.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As the operating environment of the early childhood sector is dynamic and needs to be updated from time to time, clause 51 of the Bill will provide for subsidiary legislation to effect more specific operational requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This will provide more clarity on the responsibilities of operators and centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Under the subsidiary legislation, we intend to enhance some requirements and introduce new ones to raise quality standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will continue to consult the sector on this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will take reference from sector best practices and ECDA's prevailing guidelines.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Exposure to the outdoors will be beneficial for our children in preventing the early onset of myopia.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Even as we raise standards in the sector, we will streamline certain requirements which are no longer applicable, for greater efficiency, especially those that place unnecessary administrative burden on our teachers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The sector warmly welcomed these proposals when we consulted them earlier this month.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Just as how the Bill provides requirements for the set-up of centres, the Bill also provides requirements for the orderly closure of centres, under clauses 14 and 18.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is in view that, in the past, there had been cases where centres abruptly close.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: While this has been few, the impact on parents and children involved can be quite significant.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Thus, to minimise such occurrences, ECDA will be empowered to require centres to put in place measures to ensure orderly closure.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These include giving parents and teachers advance notice of the upcoming service disruption and ceasing the enrolment of new children to the centre.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Operators have worked hard to build the trust of parents by meeting the baseline standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Today, errant operators form a small minority of the sector but they undermine the hard work of the rest of the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA takes regulatory breaches seriously and a more comprehensive and graduated penalty framework will enable ECDA to effectively and swiftly enforce requirements to safeguard the safety and well-being of our young children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: More importantly, it serves as a deterrent against errant practices and behaviours.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The type of penalty imposed eventually will depend on the severity of the breach and whether it was a repeated occurrence.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The penalty will be proportionate to the breach.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: At the same time, I would like to reassure operators that ECDA will continue to adopt a measured and developmental approach in enforcing requirements by advising centres to rectify problems.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One new regulatory sanction I would like to elaborate on is the requirement of a security deposit.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I am aware that operators are concerned about this requirement.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This security deposit is intended to spur such centres to raise their standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I encourage centres with a six-month licence to take their regulatory gaps seriously, and to rectify their breaches quickly, so as to avoid being required to put up a security deposit.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: At the same time, the Bill provides for criminal penalty for contraventions which pose a more serious risk to the safety and well-being of our children, for example, the operation of unlicensed centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The maximum fine amount has been adjusted to align with recent legislation like the Private Education Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Certain offences will be made compoundable at up to half of the maximum fine amount under clause 42.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Before ECDA determines any contraventions, its officers will investigate the cases thoroughly and establish the facts from a variety of sources.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Very often, a child may be involved in a case, which makes investigations more complex.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Hence, ECDA officers will need enhanced investigative powers to effectively carry out their duties under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These are powers similar to those available to other regulators in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As we put these powers in place, we will establish internal processes to ensure that ECDA officers carry out their investigations fairly.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I have just outlined the broad regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are expecting to commence the Act over the next year after gazetting the detailed regulatory requirements in subsidiary legislation and publishing the administrative procedures in the Codes of Practice.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Since 2015, ECDA has also been conducting sector briefings to explain and consult on the new requirements, as well as conducting customised on-site guidance for kindergartens.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, I understand that, actually, many kindergartens have already been making adjustments to prepare for the new framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: From my interactions with the sector, I am confident that almost all our operators would be able to meet these requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I believe that clear and appropriate regulatory requirements are crucial in raising standards in the early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, during my visit to Creative Thinkers Kindergarten in August last year, the principal, Ms Sakinah Dollah, shared that a clear, common understanding among the principals, teachers and support staff of ECDA's regulatory requirements will help centres to organise themselves better and to improve.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It will provide parents with greater confidence that we are making Singapore a great place to raise families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We received strong support from parents, teachers and operators on the need for this enhanced regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Bill proposes, first, a common licensing framework for childcare centres and kindergartens.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Second, all persons working in centres will need to be approved by ECDA to ensure their suitability to work with young children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In addition, there will also be clearer and more consistent requirements to guide centres in their operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA will also work with centres closely to facilitate a smooth transition.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To conclude, the proposals in the Bill will help to set a firm and consistent foundation, positioning the early childhood sector well for the future.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It complements the many, many efforts by the Government to partner the sector to improve the quality, accessibility and affordability of early childhood development services in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With that, Mdm Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While we now have more choices of operators and services, quality and standards can differ greatly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I stand in support of the Bill to further regulate the sector to improve the quality of these centres and to protect the safety and well-being of our children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But we should be mindful of compliance costs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How will ECDA mitigate against centre operators from passing on compliance costs to parents?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Both Anchor Operator and Partner Operator (POP) schemes are useful in moderating fees.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, fees of others outside of such schemes might continue to rise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will further steps be taken to moderate the costs by having more centres involved in these schemes?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Or should centres justify significant fee increases to ECDA?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, many young families have to cope with the high cost of living − anything from daily living expenses, maintenance of parents and expenses to take care of their young children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The cost impact can be quite high for the young parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Both husband and wife must work to maintain the cost of living.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Childcare centres, therefore, have become a necessity for young families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Currently, Singaporeans can enjoy a $300 basic subsidy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: From April 2013, the Government provided an additional subsidy for families with income below $7,500.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I urge the Government to give a higher subsidy during this period of economic downturn to mitigate the financial burdens of young parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There are also women who cannot take up full-time jobs due to family needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, current policies only allow non-working mothers to receive a subsidy of up to $300.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While the intention to encourage mothers to go back to work is good, many mothers have no choice but to stay at home, especially those who have to take care of their parents and young children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: What is more, there is not much flexible work in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These mothers may face even heavier financial burdens.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I hope the Government can increase the basic subsidy for non-working mothers, a gesture which can be seen as "sending coal amidst snow".

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, let me resume in English.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Another aspect of this Bill looks at ensuring holistic care and education of our children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Our war on obesity and diabetes must start with our young children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The NurtureSG taskforce has given thoughtful and important recommendations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: They include ensuring that children have adequate exercise, sleep and healthier food.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I hope these recommendations can be adopted widely because healthy lifestyles need to start at a young age.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: I hope that ECDA will require operators to provide healthy and well-balanced meals for the children under their care.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Having a "better" curriculum certainly goes beyond preparing for primary school education.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is also about life values and developing a love for learning.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Because of the centricity of early childhood education to a child's future learning, there would be value in ensuring certain core components are taught in the curriculum.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Improving the curriculum also means that teachers will have to be properly trained and equipped.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Since this Bill also provides for teachers to have greater professional standing, what kind of support will ECDA offer to smaller centres that are lacking in manpower and may face challenges in getting their teaching staff to go for courses and further training?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will centre operators also be required to review the salary of their teachers and staff and consider increasing their salaries as they become more professional?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this regard, I will speak of the three potentials of enhancing innovation, professionalism and affordability in the preschool sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But before I do so, I want to clear a nagging issue with the Minister, which has been bothering me since I read ECDA's response to the specific feedback back in November 2015.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The explanation given by ECDA to the exemption of the Ministry of Education (MOE) Kindergartens from the regulatory framework is that this is in line with the fact that the Council for Private Education regulates private education institutions under the Private Education Act, while all national schools, polytechnics and the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) come under MOE.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On what grounds should the regulation of the preschool sector be organised in a similar way as the education sector?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The two sectors are very different in purpose and pedagogies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The preschool sector entails the application of childcare skills as well as holistic education approaches that recognise the difference between early childhood development and late childhood education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Furthermore, in the education sector, the national schools serve as the primary and centralised arbiter of standards and allocation of public resources, with private schools only playing the role of augmenting public-led education to raise our young people to become productive workers, enterprising leaders and good citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the November 2015 response by ECDA, the Council for Private Education has been turned into the Committee for Private Education and absorbed into SkillsFuture Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is no equivalent in the preschool sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The pre-school sector is a lot more diverse and decentralised.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even as the Council for Private Education was no equivalent to ECDA, which regulated almost the entire preschool sector, except the few MOE kindergartens, it is certainly no equivalent now as the Committee.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: MOE is only one of the players in the preschool sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Symmetry may be beautiful, but it is wrong in this application.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What we need to ask instead are the role and function of MOE kindergartens in the preschool sector and whether the role and function, therefore, justify the exemption.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If MOE kindergartens cater to a specific constituency, say, low-income families, but seeks to be consistent in standards with the ECDC Bill and the Singapore Preschool Accreditation Framework (SPARK), then there is no justification for the exemption.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is also the strange suggestion in the ECDA public consultation response that since MOE is directly accountable to Parliament, there is no need for the inclusion of the MOE kindergartens under the regulatory framework.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Surely, Parliament cannot be expected to perform the role of ECDA, since it is a legislative body and cannot play a regulatory function to closely hold MOE kindergartens to consistent standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also a positive thing that ECDA said in its public consultation response that broad guidelines would ensure the programmes are developmentally appropriate while giving centres the flexibility to customise lesson plans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe this is a crucial stance to maintain and I would urge ECDA to keep this openness to the diversity of early childhood education models.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I also hope ECDA would consult widely with stakeholders, professional bodies and educational experts before rejecting any particular curriculum, so as to protect the diversity as much as possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The preschool sector is poised to be a field of innovation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are some interesting innovations on this front spearheaded by the Lien Foundation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is an inclusive preschool set up by Lien Foundation and the Asian Women's Welfare Association for typically developing children and children with special needs to learn and play together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is also the collaboration between Lien Foundation and the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) First Campus to develop model preschools for the heartlands and for training teachers and conducting research on early childhood education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They are not the only examples of innovation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The regulatory framework must remain broad-based and not primed for consolidating and centralising the preschool sector and ECDA must remain open-minded and consultative to continue to encourage innovation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second potential is the potential for enhancing the professionalism of early childhood educators.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is good that ECDA will be overseeing the registration of early childhood professionals and the accreditation of early childhood training programmes for now.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe it is right that ECDA gently rejected the call for an independent professional body to register the programme staff, as there is no such body that can properly perform such a task at this point in time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, having said this, I believe there is scope to aim to increase the participation of professional bodies in the registration of professionals and accreditation of the programmes, so as to develop the overall professionalism of the preschool sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is a positive thing that ECDA develops the standards for registration and course accreditation in consultation with stakeholders, representatives of the professionals and the education experts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But taking input for implementation is not the same as opening up the process to participation by the professional bodies so that these bodies could grow and develop.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The development of these professional bodies should not be neglected by ECDA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These bodies play an important role in providing platforms for the sharing of expertise and innovation and the exchange of knowledge and best practices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the spirit of Budget 2017, ECDA would do well to aim to forge and deepen partnerships with these professional bodies, so that the preschool sector could also prepare for the future economy so as to prepare our children for the future economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The third potential is the potential for enhancing the affordability of early childhood education.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Research has shown that preschool education is crucial for reducing inequality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Children who are ill-prepared and lacking the foundation for formal schooling tend to do badly in school, while putting a child in preschool improves her chances of graduating from college.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Affordable quality preschool education is, therefore, the great leveller, improving the odds of low-income families breaking out of the poverty trap.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In its public consultation response, ECDA reassured the public that regulatory costs would be low for operators who have been complying with existing regulations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is fair enough, since much of the regulatory framework is already in place and this legislation is a formalisation and consolidation of the existing regulations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this respect, I would like to call for two things.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The four family members with two dependants demographic is more aligned with the low-income family profile.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will allow more low-income families to benefit from more subsidies in a context where fees are under cost pressures to go up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: POPs complement Anchor Operators (AOPs) in keeping fees affordable while ensuring the quality of the programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Likewise, kindergartens operated by VWOs are non-profit institutions and help keep fees affordable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I do not see any reason to keep POPs and VWO operators out of KiFAS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The subsidies would not benefit the operators, only the low-income families who would have a greater selection of kindergartens to choose from.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Notwithstanding the unjustified oddity of exempting MOE kindergartens from a good regulatory framework, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In order for parents to have the added possibility of the mother returning to the workforce, the quality of the care of their children is, understandably, extremely important.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Hence, the enhanced regulatory framework to ensure excellence in care and education is crucial.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Through an enhanced regulatory framework, this Bill seeks to ensure and advance the quality of care and education in the preschool sector.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is important as more young parents in Singapore look to preschool centres for care management.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As preschool centres are geographically spread out across Singapore, centre-based care becomes more convenient and attractive to parents.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, as more women and seniors participate in the workforce, the need for quality pre­school services has increased.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is a real need to increase the support for young parents who may prefer centre-based care over care given by domestic workers or nannies.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This need to ensure quality is especially important as more parents require longer hours of care for even younger children.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What I am referring to is the shift in enrolment numbers from kindergartens to childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Kindergartens are normally half-day, while childcare centres provide longer hours.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Furthermore, the demand for infant care for children under 18 months has increased.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This trend is projected to increase in the next few years, especially since increasing centre-based infant care featured in the Budget Statement last week.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These changes necessitate an enhanced regulatory framework to ensure continued excellence in a growing and important service sector.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill seeks to maintain and advance the quality of care and education by preschool centres through various angles, with the child's well-being as a priority.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, clause 6 of this Bill introduces a licensing framework for both kinds of preschool centres.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This furthers the accountability with regard to kindergartens, which were previously able to come under a one-off registration process.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Another example is found in clause 10(3)(e), which may require licensees to undergo an audit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, clause 12 provides that a security deposit may be required and may be calibrated according to the licensee's track record and its likelihood to attract regulatory action proceedings.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This adds another accountability mechanism, this time, a financial one.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Bill also deals with the leadership of the early childhood development centre.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Under clause 8(3), it places importance on the key appointment holder's character and the fitness to operate in an application for a licence, while clause 19 ensures that this is continued by a possible disqualification of a key appointment holder.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Besides safety, quality education is ensured at multiple stages and levels, including grant of licence under clause 10(3)(b), and the educators deployed and employed under clauses 23 and 30.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill also provides for measures to help protect the children's well-being.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, clause 17 empowers the Chief Licensing Officer to issue directions to act in a certain fashion or refrain from doing something with immediate effect if there are circumstances that may endanger the safety, well-being and welfare of children or other individuals at the early childhood development centre.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Another key aspect of this Bill which I support is to ensure the reliability and continuity of the care centre.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is imperative that parents are not stuck in stressful limbo when a centre closes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, the initiative under this new law to mandate that assistance be provided to parents for alternative care placements and education arrangements, when a centre closes, is key.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is for this reason that clause 18(4)(g) is to be supported.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It contains the regulatory framework for operators of early childhood development centres.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It provides the approval framework for those performing the duties and approval framework for third-party education providers.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The Bill is also a timely and forward-looking one as it takes effect with the repeal of the Childcare Centres Act.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Section 3 states that the Bill does not apply to certain centres.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Why does this Bill not apply to preschools run by the Government, such as the MOE kindergartens?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Should it not be that standards be applied to both the Government and privately-run preschools?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: How does an agency make sure that every licensee complies with the directions and not wait until someone whistle-blows or complains?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Section 23 states the approval for performance of and deployment of individuals to perform prescribed duties.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Preschool teachers play an important role in detecting developmental issues among children.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will there be training for teachers in caring for children with special needs?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Also, the Bill does not provide much reference or guide on the qualifications and experience required for such teachers.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What other fees or charges are to be paid in respect of the services and other areas mentioned in section 51 under "Regulations"?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The interest of children should come first, ahead of industry considerations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But at the same time, if we foster an industry landscape which is effectively an oligopoly of the AOPs, POPs and MOE kindergartens, that may pose some risks in terms of losing an element of diversity and of competition.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Diversity is important, particularly in respect of centres catering to children with special needs, as I mentioned.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If so, what will be done to ensure that this takes place in a way that protects diversity and choice while also safeguarding the interests of the children?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, will other Government agencies like the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING), reach out to the sector to provide advice and the systems in respect mergers and acquisitions or alliance possibilities?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, on licensing requirements, will ECDA demonstrate flexibility on a case-by-case basis in line with the spirit of the regulations?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The case in point may be where individual teachers may possess good qualifications from institutes abroad or at home and could be required to undertake an abridged or accelerated form of the current Pre-School Qualification Accreditation Committee (PQAC) accredited advanced diploma that is required.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will ECDA practise flexibility and accept different pathways to accreditation of personnel, taking into question individual professional qualifications and their experience, or will it rigidly require all professionals to conform to the same PQAC-accredited pathway?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, will the Ministry consider setting up an independent advisory body to inform policy formulation?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This was the recommendation from a study authored by Dr Lynn Ang for the Lien Foundation in 2012 referring to the preschool sector.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And I quote from the study, "While the increasing Government involvement to regulate the sector is generally welcomed by most participants in the study, there is a concern that the overwhelming influence of Government may stifle the independent voices of preschool teachers and other stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As such, a consultative approach to policy development and implementation is seen as key in galvanising support and moving the sector forward." "One example of a consultative approach could entail the setting up of an independent advisory body comprising representatives from different key stakeholders, such as preschool teachers, service providers, teacher training providers, health professionals, family educators, community workers, social workers, parents, VWOs and other relevant agencies and experts who are involved in the care and education of young children." Madam, such a consultative approach to policy formulation recommended by experts, as I quoted above, is advisable given the rapid pace of research and innovation in this field.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the Opening of the 13th Parliament in January 2016, the Government has stated that one of its key themes is partnership.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such consultative policy formulation and implementation would demonstrate that such commitments are being honoured in practice and not only in rhetoric.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In its consultation paper of 20 November 2015, ECDA said that the MOE kindergartens are exempt because of strict oversight from MOE headquarters and because MOE is accountable to Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This seems to conflict two functions − broad oversight on the one hand and operational inspection responsibility to ensure quality standards and service delivery on the other.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If, indeed, MOE's regulation of MOE kindergartens is stricter than the standards required under the ECDA Act, that is problematic from the standpoint of equity.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If it is on par with the standards required under this Bill, will it not be more reasonable and efficient to transfer supervisory oversight over MOE kindergartens to ECDA, thus alleviating the oversight burden on the part of MOE headquarters and levelling the inspection and enforcement playing field?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Lastly, Madam, I would like to make a very exploratory suggestion.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The quality of preschool education has been shown to be a critical factor in determining educational success downstream.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This was argued by an Economist Interlligence Unit (EIU) report entitled "Starting Well" commissioned by the Lien Foundation in 2012.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We do face a challenge of inequality in Singapore with Gini coefficients above the 40 level.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These have been coming down, which is a positive development, but they are still very high by the standards of other developed countries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Not only is this right thing to do from the standpoint of social justice, not only will this help cement social solidarity and protect us from the divisive politics that is being seen in some other countries in the world today, it will also help unlock talent that could power our economic future, fire our imagination and inspire our spirits.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One of the children in a large poor family living in a Housing and Development Board (HDB) rental flat today could be the next Ron Sim or Sim Wong Hoo, the next Joseph Schooling, Yip Pin Xiu or Theresa Goh, the next Iskandar Jalil, the next Catherine Lim.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We know how important it is to ingrain good learning habits at a very young age.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Children who miss the boat because their families lack the money or understanding to invest in their preschool years will struggle in primary school and are likely to become demoralised, widening the gap with their peers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This could be why the director of a social service centre I spoke to shared that he is now seeing cases which are the children of the at-risk clients he served over 20 years ago.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is well-accepted that programmes that reward poor families for keeping their children in school can play a helpful role in breaking the poverty cycle.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The pioneering programme globally in this respect was the Bolsa Familia programme in Brazil which has inspired many similar programmes around the world.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Bolsa Familia basically incentivises, and I am saying this at the risk of some over-simplification, poor families to keep their children in school.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also well-known that many other developed countries offer partly free preschool education.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is already an initiative which the Minister launched previously, KidSTART, that can serve as the platform for a more expansionary vision here.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In other words, absenteeism by children from poor families may be very high.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such policies could include making preschool compulsory or providing some conditional benefit to parents from such families to ensure high attendance rates, which is the idea behind the Bolsa Familia policy.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I welcome this Bill as it seeks to ensure higher and consistent standards across the early childhood care education sector.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the number of young families having both parents working becomes increasingly common, the need for childcare or infant care becomes more urgent.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am glad that this Bill will give young parents assurance that the safety and welfare of their children will be protected and that the childcare centres their children attend will be professional and of high quality.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Apart from the various monetary incentives the Government has provided, I think this is a right step towards providing a more holistic approach to encourage and help young couples start their family.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The main benefit will be that young parents who send their elder child to school need not make a separate trip to send their younger child to a childcare centre.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These parents will also have the option of engaging the school bus service to send both children.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My third suggestion is also regarding staffing, which is a big issue, as many childcare centres have trouble hiring staff.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To conclude, we need to do everything we can to provide the high-quality early childhood care and education that every child deserves.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With that, Mdm Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is crucial to their development and sets the cornerstone of their adult years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is good that the Government is constantly reviewing the needs of this sector.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I support this Bill which I feel will help to improve the learning experience and development of the children in their preschool years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am pleased to note that the relevant authorities are now empowered with more investigation powers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It also should be a requirement across the board that a robust system be in place to screen all staff who work at the centres.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Background records must be accessible and up to date.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Certainly, anyone with a history of hurting children or have pedophilic tendencies must be weeded out.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Ministry will share the measures taken to do this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As with all changes, transition is often a matter of concern, especially for the smaller centres where they could be facing manpower and resource constraints to cope with the change.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share with the House how this transition period can be best managed, such that the provision of childcare and education will not be disrupted in any centre?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We are already facing childcare shortages, especially in new Build-To-Order (BTO) areas where families are younger.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill should not make the shortages worse.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This would be more efficient when a centre needs to engage providers on an ad hoc basis.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Under the same proposed rule, centres cannot give guest speakers, performers and the like any rewards without a licence.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we make this rule more flexible, as not all talents can afford to be generous with their time?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In light of the current staff shortage in the industry, those who are undergoing training should be allowed to function as relief teachers or teaching assistants.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will give them valuable hands-on exposure, while helping to ease the manpower crunch.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I note with concern that some centres are exempted from this Bill.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is it that they are unable to meet the key performance indicators?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think there should be more uniformity across schools catering to the same type of education level.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This means subjecting MOE preschools and kindergartens to the same Act, or else subjecting the private preschools and kindergartens to the same requirements as the MOE's.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, it is good to subject MOE preschools and kindergartens under this same Act.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This can ensure that whatever requested by ECDA is practical and is something that can be done.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, if there is anything that is not practical, something that needs to be fine tuned, MOE can then whisper to ECDA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Enrichment centres, therapy services, standalone playgroups, children's gyms and student care services are also exempted.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: These are common places where children are sent to for learning and to be cared for.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, their staff should also be registered.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Both the parents and childcare centres are concerned about whether they will be affected by the new regulations.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, if a smaller centre did not apply for a permit in time, will the authorities help them to make sure that students are not affected?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, some centres are exempted from this Bill including MOE kindergartens.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Why are MOE kindergartens not regulated under this Bill?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that these kindergartens already have a set of stringent rules in place but consumers may feel that the Government did not apply the same standard, or that some kindergartens are better than the others.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I feel that there should be uniformity when it comes to educating children of the same age.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, centres under MOE should set an example to make sure that ECDA's requirements are practical and reasonable.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Other types of pre-school education centres, such as children's gyms and enrichment centres, are also exempted from the Bill.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Government stipulate a set of simpler rules to protect the children when they are at these places, too?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Together with about 500 kindergartens, they provide preschool services so that our children can receive quality care and education in their foundation years.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Amongst them, there are small and medium enterprises as well as bigger ones with more than 10 branches each.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Regardless of the scale, it is important that all operators deliver high levels of professional care and services.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The tightening of the regulatory framework to raise centre quality by safeguarding the well-being of the children and, to a certain extent, the staff, is to be applauded.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the union, we, too, received complaints against the management of childcare centres by early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These concern issues with regard to salaries and even abdication of responsibilities by the management.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These incidents serve as reminders on the need for a rigorous system to ensure that lapses in management can be detected early or prevented.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I feel that we do need to avoid some unintended consequences and strengthen work in other areas.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is disconcerting to the educators if it is perceived that operators command the rights and can transfer all or a majority of the responsibilities to their staff.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, I urge the Ministry and the trade association to take a firm stance against operators who do so.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We, in the union, stand ready to work with the Ministry and trade association to work out proper guidelines when operators conduct checks and inquiries.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the same time, I hope the licensing framework also takes into account where there is evidence of unfair treatment meted out by the operators against their staff.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Furthermore, sudden and unexpected closure of centres have also resulted in loss of income for the teachers and staff.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this context, the Ministry can coordinate with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) or the union to find out more details.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many of them are genuine in wanting to provide and deliver professional quality care to their children.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We should not end up with only big players who are the only ones who can meet the requirements.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the Ministry and trade association can work together to assist smaller operators transform their operations, not just to meet the higher compliance requirements but also to ensure that their staff upgrade, their operations are streamlined and they take advantage of available technology.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I can understand that operators need additional resources and time towards putting in place administrative tracking to fulfil the compliance requirements.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that under the strategies identified by the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE), assistance will be available to help centre operators do more with the same resources.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This should help to bring about significant improvements in the overall efficiency for both the operators as well as the sector.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I congratulate the Ministry for a well-thought through piece of legislation, and commend the effort to engage all stakeholders in the process of drafting this Bill.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In this regard, I hope that the Ministry will consider seriously some suggestions on the planning of preschool centres.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On top of setting high standards and enforcement measures for operations, health, safety and teaching methods, we ought to recognise that our preschool centres cannot help families effectively if they are not there where and when they are needed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will ensure that there will be sufficient places for the enrolment of children in the estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More often than not, the building of flats and childcare centres/kindergartens does not take place concurrently and parents would have to opt for other childcare centres around their neighbourhood, most of which may also be located further away.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For a few housing estates with high childcare demand, the long waiting list for the choice childcare centres is a great source of frustration amongst parents.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More and more families these days have both parents who are working.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We cannot assume that there is a grandparent or domestic helper available in every household to take care of the child in the event that there is no vacancy.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, we must consider the role of grandparents who are involved in childcare.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Often, these grandparents are the ones who send their grandchildren to school.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will promote a more active lifestyle amongst the preschool children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: By learning the importance of healthy eating and exercising, the children would be able to inculcate these good habits from young.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hopefully, these measures will decrease the number of obese children entering Primary school in the future.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: These days, most young families are dual-income, and children would be placed with the childcare centres very early in their lives.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In the past, children are placed at the childcare centres for shorter hours, like those equivalent to a play school or a kindergarten.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Today, the role of these childhood development centres have expanded both in terms of the scope and extent of caregiving.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Many centres are not simply learning and interactive grounds for our young infants, but also seen as a preparatory school before they begin formal education.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With more demand, different options of child-minding facilities have emerged over the years.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, often, there are inconsistencies among the operators.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With parents placing more responsibilities and expectations on our centres, it is thus necessary to have a framework that regulates and guides the basic operations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I see this effort as a first step to ensure the minimum standards amongst operators in order to facilitate an equivalent early childhood development centre.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In doing so, there will be a few areas where potential concerns may arise, and I seek the clarifications from the Minister, and would like to provide some suggestions.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: While it is understandable to have a range of prices from different centres that cater to varying groups and it is the parents' choice to decide what best meets the needs of their child, the affordability of these centres must always remain accessible to a broad group of children.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Under current conditions, there is already a shortage of certified persons who can perform duties in a childcare centre.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For some centres, the intake of the children is much lesser than the enrolment capacity allowed as they have insufficient staff-to-student ratio.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As I understand it, sometimes, the intake was managed in accordance with the availability of staff to ensure that each child can safely progress from nursery to kindergarten within the same centre.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Depending on the allowable duties specified subsequently, this may further worsen the staffing situation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Can the ratio of non-teaching staff be increased to assist the teachers with the workload of having to care, teach and manage the administrative tasks?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: An appropriate balance can be made in accordance with the classes of licence that will be issued.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I believe this may help to strike a better balance, create employment and relieve some of our short-term staffing shortages in the industry.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In this Bill, there is no mention on the frequency of audits and whether a standard checklist will be made available for the centre's staff to have information documented and prepared on an ongoing basis.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This will help reduce the administrative load and preparation time of our centres when it comes to audit as they are usually operating close to 5.5 days each week.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As much as we hope this will not happen to any of the centres, but pre-emptive measures must be taken to safeguard the children and staff.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Both the staff and parents will need assistance and adequate time to look for alternatives, if available.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With the current vacancy limitation, finding a suitable alternate arrangement may prove to be a tall challenge.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Businesses of third-party education service providers have flourished in the preschool sector over the past few years.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: While there is nothing wrong in providing options and variety for children to learn, the approach in which it is offered has created inequality amongst the children.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Today, in many centres, these additional curricula are optional classes.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Sometimes, the classes are held within the centre and, other times, at external locations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The issue is that not all families can afford to send their children for additional classes.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: These children often have to sit out or take rest breaks while seeing their friends continue to be engaged and learning.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is unknown to us what psychological effect this may have on a young child.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Furthermore, we should not be practising differing standards on the children at that tender age.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Thus, I urge the Ministry to reconsider if there is a need to have additional classes conducted by third-party service providers, unless the learning opportunity is given to every child enrolled.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The framework that we seek to introduce here will be a step in the right direction.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I hope this will bring about more consistency and give our parents some peace of mind.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify under what circumstances would an audit be required?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do understand that ECDA already conducts such audits and the officers generally visit centres at least once a year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why not then codify this into the Bill?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In cases where a security deposit is required, can the Minister clarify under what circumstances will the security deposit be forfeited?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, can the Minister provide a range of the amounts of security deposit required?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thirdly, the requirement of a licensee to give the CLO prior notice before ceasing operations or surrendering a licence is a good mechanism in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This gives parents time to search for alternative ECDCs for their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many Members in this House have also shared the same concern.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While ECDA has provided explanations publicly about this, I urge the Minister to reconsider as it does seems like there are double standards here.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This new Act should apply to all parties, regardless of whether they are operated privately or by the Government.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, Mdm Speaker, I understand that, on curriculum, we will continue to provide broad guidelines to ensure that programmes are developmentally appropriate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I urge the Minister to ensure that we do not become too focused on academics.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are children who are under seven years old.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I see that there are already assessment books for kindergarten children and I see that there are already tuition classes for them as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must remember that for these children, play is important and perhaps should be the focus of our ECDCs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Dr David Whitebread from the University of Cambridge stated in his paper "The importance of play" that: "What is increasingly recognised within the research and policy communities, however, is that one vital ingredient in supporting healthy intellectual, emotional and social development in young children is the provision of opportunities and the support for play." His view is also supported by the European Parliament which, on 12 May 2011, adopted a resolution on "Early Years Learning" in the European Union, which notes that the early years of childhood are critical for children's development and highlights that "in addition to education, all children have the right to rest, leisure and play".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that this is the direction we are heading in, that we remember that they are kids after all, and kids need to play.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot legislate that parents spend time with their children nor can we legislate that parents impart the rights values to their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is entirely up to us parents, and the lessons we teach our children are far more important than the lessons in school.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ultimately, children copy what their parents do and it is their parents' behaviours that shape theirs the most.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot spend every minute with our children but perhaps an important time is bedtime.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My daughter's favourite bedtime story is "The things I love about bed time".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I must have read this story close to 100 times now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On Sunday night, she fell asleep after I read her this story and, for the first time, I read the notes for parents and caregivers at the end of the book.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should have read that much earlier but, at least, I am honest.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It said, "spending time with your child as they prepare for bed is a wonderful opportunity to develop and maintain a close and loving bond.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Playing a fun bedtime game, sharing a story, listening to them recount their favourite moments of the day, discussing dreams and future events they are looking forward to, praising them for a task well done, and telling them how much you love them − all of these things create an environment in which your child will feel happy, safe, secure, loved and valued.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Ultimately, these are simple rituals that contribute to an increase in the positive emotion of your child.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For you as the parent, this is precious time in which you can be consciously and constructively be involved in building a positive state of mind.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Your child will hopefully internalise this optimism and it will guide them on a path to a full and happy life." I have to admit that I wished I had read more bedtime stories to my daughter and, in writing this speech, it made me reflect on this and I hope that all parents think about this as well, about how important a role we play as parents and teachers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I look forward to reading this book another hundred more times to my daughter and another 200 hundred times to my twins.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, I read them both this story this morning and they probably heard the story many times already when they were in my wife's womb.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They were so eager to come into this world that they came two months early.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These two little girls gave us quite a scare last week and, to be honest, it has not been an easy week.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have actually told the twins that last year, I asked Minister Heng whether he can backdate the start of the First Step Grant which was announced during Budget 2016.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I told the twins that the Minister said "no" and so, I urged them to please be born after the Committee of Supply (COS) Debates, after any new parenthood policies are announced.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On a positive note, I now have three daughters whose birthdays are about a week apart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, we can have one birthday party for three kids.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We must remember this quote by George Santayana, and it reads: "A child educated only at school is an uneducated child." Mdm Speaker, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our childcare centres and kindergartens are as varied as the uniforms, or lack of, for the children in their care.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a wide range of fees, programmes and facilities.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, the Bill does not address how the Ministry will ensure that centres charge reasonable fees.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some centres claim that they offer unique, high-quality programmes and charge fees which can match our universities' tuition fees.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although this is a free market, some degree of control by the Ministry would be helpful.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I was reassured to find out that new administrative requirements are clear and will not be too onerous upon the operators.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Operators should have no difficulty adhering to the new regulations, minimising operational inefficiencies and costs, while safeguarding centre quality and standards.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Notwithstanding, I would like to ask the Minister whether operators will be expected to employ designated operation, administrative or compliance staff to ensure that they are running their centres according to the new framework.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, such audits are conducted at least once a year.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am also concerned about the impact of temporary centre closures in the event of disease outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are clear conditions under which centres will be permitted to start running again.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, during the closures, many families will be left in difficulty, due to more dual-income families and grandparents staying in the workforce longer.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Finding someone or somewhere to take care of their children will be a big challenge.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope the Ministry will address this and share what contingency plans it has for such situations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Embracing such children and helping them to integrate into the preschool community should be the way forward, instead of segregating them.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If the parents feel confident enough to enrol them, it means that their conditions are usually manageable with some conditional help and empathy.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While they will need extra care and concern, if the Ministry can facilitate operators' partnership with referred specialists, the interests of these children will be safeguarded.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This has led to the flourishing of the early childhood education landscape where parents can send their children to different schools with different pedagogies that cater to differing needs, wants and aspirations.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Over time, however, that has led to an adverse impact where children, depending on their social economic status, could possibly have different starting points in life depending on the preschool, kindergarten or childcare centre that they attend.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I see the amendments proposed in the Bill as a positive step where the Government is sticking to its light-touch approach, yet, at the same time, adjusting the system so that it continues to serve the broad interests of the community by offering diversity and choice to parents.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would now like to touch on three amendments to the Bill that I think resonate with me the most.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Aside from having a well-developed curriculum that emphasises learning through exploration and play, the quality of educators is perhaps the next most important factor that determines whether children will have an enriching early childhood education.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad that the Bill will strengthen what the Minister calls a robust regulatory framework on the operations of an ECDC.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This, in my opinion, will complement the on-going initiatives to elevate the service standards of the industry.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, it is mandatory for all teachers and allied educators to undergo supervised training so that they have the proper qualifications to teach in a preschool.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It would thus be appropriate to impose a similar regulatory framework to curb the proliferation of schools that are not run by licensed operators.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the same spirit of creating a stronger safeguard, I would urge the Government to consider defining and clarifying what constitutes an ECDC.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would home-based classes that focus on delivering structured curriculum be considered an ECDC under the Bill?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or would enrichment centres that conduct speech and drama classes or creative thinking for preschoolers be considered as ECDCs?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
