text: How would specialised set-ups, such as those providing occupational therapy or unique training for special needs children, be classified?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is important for us to be granular in our approach and define in unambiguous terms what an ECDC is.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the current moment, there are several avenues and channels for aspiring early childhood educators to get trained in the field.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Presently, aspiring early childhood educators can get trained at early childhood diploma programmes in the polytechnics and via training provided at the SEED Institute.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In line with the SkillsFuture initiative and the CFE's recommendation to acquire and utilise deep skills, I hope that there will be more avenues for our aspiring early childhood educators to be trained.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my opinion, mid-career switchers can be a valuable source of manpower to a sector that is currently experiencing a labour crunch.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, many mid-career executives are parents themselves, and they can bring with them important parenting skills that can help improve the overall standards of care and classroom delivery.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Aside from creating training platforms for early childhood educators to attain the much needed foundational skills, I hope that the Government can put in place some form of continuous education programme so that our educators can continue to upgrade their skill set over time and be in sync with the latest teaching methods and pedagogies.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is especially important for those who wish to deepen their career in the field and eventually take on a leadership role in their respective schools and it is also in line with our SkillsFuture initiative and the CFE's strategic thrust mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Specialised continuous education will create multiple pathways of career progression by giving early childhood educators the platform to hone and deepen their skills in specific areas of interest, such as pedagogy development, developmental psychology, or even early childhood assessment and intervention.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The deepening of skillsets will naturally allow these educators to have meaningful career progression and be paid a higher wage when they become specialists in their field.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: ECDCs, in their course of operations, will inevitably work with third-party education service providers to offer enrichment or physical education programmes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Children are exposed to higher risk of getting hurt when they attend classes conducted by these unqualified trainers and it is important that we assess all such trainers thoroughly to minimise such risk.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe these amendments will align the sector towards achieving a common standard while the sector moves towards attaining a higher quality of service.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a parent of two young children, I am heartened and reassured by the amendments in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a Parliamentarian, I conclude my speech in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Clearly, it is without a doubt that many of us recognise the importance of early childhood development, not just because we are parents but a lot of studies have shown the impact that good development work can have on children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The Member, Mr Louis Ng, reminded all of us that it is not just from the ECD, but really, at home as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something important for us to remember.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A fair number of points raised here do not pertain to the Bill, but they are important points with regard to the importance of the early childhood effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I will address some of these subsequently in a few days' time during the COS debates; others, I will address them on other occasions.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But I will take the opportunity to make some general points to address some of the perspectives highlighted by some Members.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I will illustrate later, MOE plays a very significant role in developing the curriculum and learning pedagogies and the rest of the industry take reference from it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is also important to note that this whole set-up is not just driven from the top.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There is a lot of effort in engaging the various stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We cannot do it without that, because it is a very varied space and there are many different schools of thought.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some of the examples that Mr Leon Perera highlighted, for example, from Lien Foundation and the many different trials that are ongoing, these are strongly supported by ECDA.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do want to explore the different ways of education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: You may not want a single approach, because there are many different schools of thought.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They are effective in different ways and they are effective for different children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We want to see how these different curricula can play out, how we can implement it, and how we can scale it, not necessarily across the board.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In some instances, we want to scale it across the board; in some instances, in very boutique areas where it addresses the needs of specific children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the special needs sector, one of the concerns highlighted was whether, as a result of these moves, it would impact some of the smaller players.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: From a purely intellectual and theoretical basis, I would agree that it would sound sensible to allow a thousand flowers to bloom and to have many different players.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But having a very practical perspective on this, from dealing with the industry with many different players, I would say that the reality is not quite the same.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I visited a number of them; very interesting programmes but, unfortunately, probably not able to scale up because a lot of its success is centred around the person who is driving the programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is very manpower-intensive, which may be difficult to scale.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We want to be able to encourage some of these centres to continue.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But there are also childcare centres which leave much room for improvement and really do need to level up.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, I would agree that we want to encourage experimentation, but we also want to ensure that our children receive a good standard of education and care, which is the main objective of this effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is an important sector, which is why we are doing what we are doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is important to engage all the different players.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is also important for us to explore but, at the same time, have a certain structure and approach, and that is the way we have taken it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I am very heartened and encouraged by the strong recognition by all of you on the importance of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Notwithstanding the various comments, Members clearly recognise that there is that need to ensure higher and more consistent quality standards across the early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This can be done without necessarily squeezing out some of the smaller players.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I am sure that many of our early childhood professionals and operators are similarly encouraged.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We did not want to drive it down from the top; many different stakeholders have been consulted.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Where there were areas of concern, we have gone back and forth for a slightly longer period of time to take on board their feedback.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What I am encouraged by is, like many Members, many of the stakeholders are strongly supportive of us taking this step.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I believe that this Bill is a step in the right direction, because we do need to give every child a good start and to make Singapore a good place to raise families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On a point raised by Assoc Prof Daniel Goh with regard to lower-income children, I would completely agree that early childhood is important for all children, but for children who come from particularly challenged backgrounds, it becomes even more critical.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is also why we set up ECDA.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We realise that in those early years, for those of us who are able to provide our children with exposure and development, our children are able to grow and develop well before they reach primary school.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But we realise that there is a gap.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For some of the children who come from more disadvantaged backgrounds, they enter Primary 1 with a fairly significant gap from the rest of their peers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The way we have structured subsidies also seeks to ensure that lower-income families will not end up not sending their children to preschool because they cannot afford it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Even down to a couple of dollars, children will be able to attend some of these establishments.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But we intend to see it through and expand it; this is where it is not just in terms of the ECDC itself, but actually an all-encompassing approach to see how we hand-hold and work with the families along the journey.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, I want to assure the Members of this House that there is very little doubt in our minds about the importance of this effort and especially the work to be done with the lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Christopher de Souza remarked that the Bill is much needed and timely.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A sound and robust regulatory framework guides centres and safeguards the sector against errant practices and behaviours.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This sets a strong foundation for the sector to further innovate teaching and learning practices and to develop higher quality programmes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many of the smaller centres appreciate the fact that some of these guidelines and parameters are set, as these allow them to bring themselves up to a higher standard, because they do not have the scale or the resources necessary to level themselves up on their own.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For instance, Miss Cheryl Chan suggested considering alternatives to paper qualifications when determining staff suitability.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh suggested increasing the participation of professional bodies in the registering of professionals and accreditation of programmes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: He also suggested that it is important for us to consider those who have qualifications from overseas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing suggested a new training institute to ensure sufficient teachers in the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Indeed, we share our Members' concerns on the manpower constraints and this is one area we are paying very close attention to.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many of these initiatives have been co-created with partners, such as SkillsFuture Singapore, preschool operators, industry and professional associations and the union.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We note Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's suggestion for greater participation of professionals in the process of accrediting training courses and qualifications.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is already done in the development of teacher registration and course accreditation standards where our early childhood professional representatives and subject matter experts are invited to provide their expertise.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to recognising those who have qualifications from overseas, we do encourage the respective childcare centres and kindergartens to put forward the names of these individuals so that we can evaluate them on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To echo Mr Darryl David's emphasis, in fact, many are mid-career entrants.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: No matter what we do in this sector, frankly, without people, this is not going to work.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The response has been encouraging, but we are not letting up on that front.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We need to keep up at making sure that we not only bring in numbers but ensure the quality of the people who are coming in as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many of them are very passionate, the mid-career ones especially, because they have reached a stage of their lives where they are looking at doing something different.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some of them are parents themselves who recognise the importance of early childhood development, and we really welcome them on board the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the teaching staff, including infant educarers, ECDA has, in recent years, moved to open alternate entry pathways for them to upgrade professionally.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is something that Miss Cheryl Chan raised and we will continue to move in this direction.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will touch more on these efforts to support the manpower needs of the sector, to provide more accessible, affordable and quality pre-school places at the upcoming COS debates.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On curriculum requirements, some Members, such as Mr Desmond Choo, noted that our preschool sector provides a diverse range of programmes for parents to choose from, so as to best cater to their preferences and the different needs of their young children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Under the Bill, we will continue requiring centres to have programmes that are age-appropriate and holistic.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh would be glad to know that within the regulatory framework, centres will continue to have the flexibility to innovate and customise their specific curriculum to suit the needs of the children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For good practices, we will be more than happy to take them on board and see how best to introduce them to more establishments.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the examples cited, ECDA has certainly supported many of these ideas and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As a reference, centres can refer to MOE's Nurturing Early Learners Curriculum Framework when designing and implementing their kindergarten curriculum.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Learning through play is a key component for the framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For those who are concerned that we are over-schoolifying the whole process − no, we are very mindful that play is a very important part of early childhood development.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, MOE is a very important player in this whole effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They are driving the curriculum framework development; again, not only on their own, but also leveraging on the experiences of other subject matter experts on this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And certainly play is a very key component of their emphasis as well, which is why MOE has stepped in to look at MOE Kindergarten as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And I will address the issue later with regard to their exemption.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the early years, of three years old and below, centres can refer to ECDA's Early Years Development Framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This framework also takes a strong alignment with the MOE framework.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to nutritional and outdoor physical time requirements highlighted by some Members, I agree with Mr Desmond Choo that increasing access to healthier food options for preschool children will help them develop good dietary habits for life.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We should do that at home, and not just depend on the preschool.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do what we can at preschool, but home is where it all starts.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is very important to remember that I do not need a Bill for good parenting to take place, and, frankly, the best influences come at home.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I also second Mr Louis Ng's point that we should provide more opportunities for children to play.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As mentioned earlier, play is a very central focus in the curriculum, especially playing outdoors.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Studies have shown clearly that having outdoor activities makes a lot of difference in terms of preventing myopia, and in developing a more resilient and hardier population.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I have earlier explained, this Bill will also provide for subsidiary legislation to be gazetted.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Members have highlighted how do we do this, that or the other?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A lot of these will come in the form of subsidiary legislation that will be gazetted.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Certainly, the suggestions that have been put forward today will be taken on board as we finalise some of these detailed requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Of course, there are concerns that many Members have raised and I am fully aware that there will be challenges.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When you put in place new measures, it is not an effortless process.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But it is an important one and stakeholders recognise it; centres recognise that it is necessary, and they have also flagged out their concerns to us.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This was expressed by many Members, including Ms Thanaletchimi, Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Darryl David, Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Yee Chia Hsing, Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Mr Ang Hin Kee, Mr Louis Ng and Mr Leon Perera.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Many of these concerns have also been expressed during our many different consultation sessions with the public and the operators.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: One, which Mr Leon Perera specifically highlighted, was whether the higher cost will impact on the continued operations, and whether this is compelling a consolidation of centres, and forcing some of the smaller players to close, especially those catering to children with special needs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Does it, in turn, translate into higher fees for parents and administrative burdens on operators and teachers?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the closure aspect, we expect most kindergartens would smoothly transit to the new Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have reached out to many different players, including the smaller ones.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They recognise the importance and some of the challenges.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Since 2015, many kindergartens, with the support of ECDA, have already started making preparations to meet the new licensing requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Our whole effort is not about penalising and weeding out the smaller players.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is actually about helping those in the industry who are passionate about educating our children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: How do we help them to level up?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is very much, as I have mentioned earlier, a developmental approach that we are taking.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That said, there will be closures because, every year, we do have a number of kindergartens and childcare centres that will close or have a change in licensees for various business reasons.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some kindergartens also convert to childcare centres to better serve the needs of parents.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Just a very quick note, we work very closely also with the special needs sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are working very closely with many of the special needs centres, and many of them do not have a huge concern in transiting to this new regime.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, many of the very progressive and interesting childcare centres and kindergartens are trying out different types of approaches.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, many of them are fairly well-run, which is why, in many ways, they are doing what they are doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These establishments do not have a problem transiting to the new regime under this Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA is also undertaking many other initiatives to support the sector in this whole transition process.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To continue, as we have mentioned, affordability remains a key cornerstone of our whole approach.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, ensuring quality and affordable early childhood development services for parents remains paramount.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Apart from broad-based support that ECDA has been providing to the sector to meet the new requirements, I would like to assure Members that we will take a gradual and calibrated approach.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some Members have raised the issue of potential fee increases arising from the higher requirements and their impact on families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Indeed, common wisdom would highlight that there is a trade-off between being cheap, good and fast.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, some Members have also asked, "Why are we doing inspections once a year?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Let's do it twice a year." So, there is a balance needed.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We recognise a need to ensure standards and to level up the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: At the same time, how do you balance that against onerous requirements?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As can be seen from Members' inputs, there will be tensions, and trade-offs will invariably be done.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As we have highlighted in CFE, it is about the doing.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have been practising that in terms of ECDA's engagement with the sector, and we have been able to put this into practice as far as we can and, at the same time, not compromising on quality.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA has field-tested the requirements on a variety of centres, both large and small, to see how it can be operationalised.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are quite assured that it should pretty much unfold in that direction.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For those who do have challenges, we will work closely with them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Louis Ng highlighted that centres will need to undergo regular assessments before their licence renewals to demonstrate that they have maintained their standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We encourage centres to meet the standards and, if they do, they can have a three-year licence.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In addition, ECDA will continue to conduct unannounced audits.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested we should do more audits.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For those who have challenges, we will pay closer attention, and we will visit them more often to help them level up their standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But we do need to strike a balance and I think Members appreciate that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I have mentioned earlier, many of the new requirements have already been implemented as part of the sector's best practices.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Hence, it is not as if with the introduction of this Bill, a whole new slew of initiatives is coming in.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Actually, many of these have been unfolding in various forms in the past couple of years.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, ECDA's advisory recommends centres to have air purifiers during haze periods.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA is looking into making this requirement in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We believe that the prevailing requirements are adequate in our current context.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Some flexibility has also been catered for these requirements, as new requirements are added.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, Miss Cheryl Chan suggested allowing non-teaching staff to support teachers more.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I mentioned earlier that there is no reason why the operational staff cannot help trained teachers supervise outdoor play time.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Centres can also use neighbourhood playgrounds to fulfil their outdoor space requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, ECDA has even gone down to help centres look at how to manage their costs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, for the requirement on first-aid kits, ECDA has looked into the items and the quantity of each item.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: While the first-aid kit items are not going to drive costs up in a significant way, ECDA has gone into details to work with various centres, especially the smaller ones, who are reaching out because they do not have the resources and the set-up to look at some of the good practices in detail.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In addition to these, given that affordability is a concern to many parents, ECDA has also ramped up the supply of more quality and affordable places.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something I have been talking about regularly, and this includes more places offered by AOPs and POPs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have also made subsidy enhancements in recent years, and we note Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's suggestion to expand the support given, especially for lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is something that we completely agree is important.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: A lot of it will come under the KidSTART effort, which is something that I have mentioned before.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We intend to make sure that it succeeds and takes off on a more extensive basis.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Desmond Choo asked for the Government to have some degree of control over fees to ensure that fees are affordable to parents.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For the remaining operators, we see the need for operators to determine their own fees, as their programmes may have different cost structures and they may need to adjust their fees from time to time to ensure business sustainability.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This will help to ensure that fee increases are done in a transparent and fair manner.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the affordability of fees, that will be dealt with separately and I will talk about that in the COS debates.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These are the finer regulatory details, such as field trips, supplementary enrichment activities and to make enrichment activities optional, which means centres must continue to provide classes for children who do not opt for these programmes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This approach creates greater flexibility and fee transparency for parents, allowing parents to make informed choices and manage their costs better.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Administrative workload is something that many of us are concerned about.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is a valid concern and something that we are very mindful of as we embark on this journey with this Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We certainly want teachers to spend more quality time on our children than on administration.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: When you speak to teachers, what they want to do is to teach, not to spend time doing administration.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But we also realise that to run a system in a systematic way, where you not just teach well but are also able to replicate that on a sustainable basis, you need structures and processes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Hence, it is important for us to not run away from that, but to make sure that it is not onerous.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA has taken a focused effort to streamline administration and make it flexible, as I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For example, over the past year, we have been working with the sector to streamline the new regulatory standards checklist for operators' own preparatory self-assessments, so that they know what to look out for.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Most operators should be able to manage the new framework with their existing resources.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have spoken to many of them, in terms of how they envisage themselves adapting to address the needs of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Besides streamlining the regulatory standards checklist, ECDA has also released a series of very useful templates that centres can use to guide and track their day-to-day operations.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA will also be enhancing its information technology (IT) systems to allow centres to interface with ECDA more seamlessly on regulatory matters.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Technology can go some way to make this more efficient and easier for centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We agree with Mr Ang Hin Kee's suggestion on the value of tapping on technology to keep costs down and free up teachers' time for our children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Beyond streamlining requirements, ECDA has collaborated with the Association for Early Childhood and Training Services and the Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore to identify smart solutions to help teachers with their daily administrative duties, such as temperature and attendance taking.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As we embark on the journey towards Smart Nation, it should encompass all manners of activities that we are undertaking.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These solutions were showcased at the Early Childhood Conference in September last year, and many operators have signed up since.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the exclusion of MOE kindergartens, Ms Thanaletchimi, Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Louis Ng raised the question about why MOE is excluded.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: ECDA is an agency that is overseen by MOE and MSF.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Both Ministries take a very active interest and role in shaping this space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is the reason why ECDA was set up.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are very clear that the formative years are vital.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have in place our primary, secondary, tertiary education, and so on.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: What we have prior to ECDA was a space which was left to the market.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We thought it was important for us to step in.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is why it is not just an MOE effort, but both MOE and MSF are stepping into that space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MOE continues to drive the curriculum in very significant ways; MOE is not just focused on primary school education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There is a need to look at the pedagogy that is involved leading up to that stage.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As a result of being involved in MOE kindergartens, MOE is also looking at how that whole continuum extends into the early primary school years, including how to harmonise this whole effort and how that streamlines into the longer-term development effort for education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MOE is not a fringe player coming in, or one of those small establishments that has no background.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They have been intimately involved in the process from Day 1.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The ECDC Act is intended to regulate the standards of private kindergartens and childcare providers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The MOE kindergartens are run directly by the Government, and they have an Act that governs it, similar to the way MOE runs primary and secondary schools and junior colleges.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is not to say that MOE runs their kindergartens the same way that primary schools are run.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: They should be run differently; the approach is different.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The MOE kindergartens will continue to be regulated under the Education Act, along with other national schools.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is an approach similar to how we approach the other parts of the education space.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MOE maintains strict oversight of the MOE kindergartens and will be directly accountable, as they are accountable to this House, with regard to broader education.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On the one hand, Members feel that bringing them on board under the ECDC Bill would be sensible, and I can understand that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On the other hand, there is another Act that is already governing them.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: MOE is also intimately involved, and they will meet the requirements that are demanded of the rest of the other centres as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We agree that sufficient time is needed for parents to look for alternatives.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In determining the notification period, ECDA must strike a balance between the feasibility of the time period for centres – because there are real practical concerns from their perspective as well, and centres would not wish to prematurely alarm parents – against the need for early warning.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will see how we can work that out.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To Ms Thanaletchimi's question, we will maintain the prevailing professional qualification requirements and this information is available on ECDA's website for all to refer to.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I mentioned earlier, for those who have other qualifications that do not quite fit, if the centre feels that they want to put the person forward, the centre can do so and we can look at it on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To clarify on Mr Darryl David's point on third-party enrichment vendor staff suitability, we will start by making simple assessments of these individuals' track record.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do not intend to specify any professional qualifications required of these individuals, since these enrichment classes are optional and encompass a very wide range of niche activities from sports, drama to cooking to whatever it may be.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It will not be addressed within this Bill, but it is something that we will look at and work with the sector to see to what degree we want to define the requirements for some of these individuals concerned.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I note Mr Gan Thiam Poh's concern on the impact of temporary closures arising from disease outbreaks on parents.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: To support working parents, the Government has also enhanced child and infant care leave provisions over the years.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Should there be a need in the future, this approach can be reviewed and we are open to it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The security bond may be forfeited as a form of regulatory sanction against breaches, as provided for under clause 16.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I note some of the other issues in the early childhood sector that were raised by Members.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As I mentioned, some of these are beyond the scope of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Regarding more support for centres and early childhood teachers caring for children with special needs, as raised by some Members, ECDA and my Ministry will continue to work with training institutes and education providers to equip preschool teachers with the necessary skills to support children with developmental needs, such as rolling out professional development courses for in-service preschool teachers who want to enhance their skills in this area.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are quite assured that for centres that are operating in this space, transiting to the new arrangement should not be a problem.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On the concerns whether putting in place some of these requirements will force some of these special needs centres to go out of busines, that is very unlikely to happen.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On the co-location of centres with primary schools, as raised by Mr Yee Chia Hsing, many of the MOE kindergartens are already located within primary schools, bringing convenience to parents who have children in both MOE kindergartens and the primary schools that they are located in.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: That is the approach that MOE is looking at with regard to the MOE kindergartens.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: On employment terms and disputes between centres and their teachers, as raised by Mr Ang Hin Kee, we thank Mr Ang and the Education Services Union for the good work in supporting our early childhood teachers who found themselves caught in unfortunate circumstances.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Early childhood professionals could also approach MOM to file a complaint against violations of the Employment Act.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These concerns are important as they support the overall functioning of the sector as well as some of the points that I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But the Bill focuses on ensuring children's safety, well-being and welfare in centres.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Again, just to reiterate, we do not need a Bill to make sure that we raise strong families.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that all of us can do.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It takes a whole nation to play a part.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: If we are able to put our hearts and soul into this, both at home and in the sector, we have every reason to be optimistic for our future.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Because once you lay a strong foundation, there is a high probability and a good chance that our young children can grow up to be responsible citizens and contribute back significantly to our nation.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Once again, I thank Members of this House for their support of this Bill and the very meaningful debate today.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Just two brief clarification questions to the Minister.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The first is just to be a bit more specific on the requirements for licensing of personnel within the early childhood sector.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: For those individuals who have strong qualifications either from abroad or locally, would the Ministry actually consider an abridged or accelerated version of the PQAC-accredited advance diploma to allow them to serve?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The second clarification is really in regard to the point I raised about absenteeism.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If such a system is not already in place, would Ministry consider requiring early childhood centres to flag out to the Ministry children who are persistently absent as potential candidates for KidSTART when that programme is expanded in the future?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the first, indeed, we will look at the individuals' qualifications that may not fit our criteria today, especially qualifications from overseas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will look at whether, in their case, a more truncated or accelerated programme is possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There is a balance that needs to be struck.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: But it is something that we are open to looking at.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to the second question, it is a very important one.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is important for us to realise that part of the challenge is that while we may make some of these schemes and subsidies available, the challenge is with the children's attendance.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Because you will find that for some families, and for a range of reasons – there is not one reason particularly – intermittent attendance is actually worrying.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: The opportunities for development and exposure are there for the children, but for whatever reasons, the children do not attend.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do know some of the factors that are involved.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In fact, this is something that I am quite particular about personally.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As part of our effort with KidSTART, working with the families, it is not just about the children, it is about the family, too.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, addressing absenteeism, ensuring the children have regular attendance in preschools will be a very important component of this effort.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Once we are able to do that, it will go a very long way.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is not just about working on the children.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Mr Dennis Tan, please keep your clarification short.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the new regulations lead to increased compliance cost which may, in turn, lead to increased fees payable by parents?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am asking this because, currently, I think the existing fees are already a burden to many parents and I would like to know how the Ministry will manage this.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In the process of coming up with this Bill, we have been working very closely with the industry on how to unfold this, how these various measures would kick-in in very practical terms.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Childcare centres today, for example, already operate under a licensing regime.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We have already embarked on that journey, and many of these players are already quite far on that journey.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are now, in some sense, formalising it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are very mindful as we implement this new Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Even as we implement this, the requirements are not cast in stone now.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Along the way, there may be push-back from the industry as certain unknown processes may turn out to be more cumbersome than they need to be and they add to costs.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: For this, we will look at it and see how to best calibrate it.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is important, and I would say this, because I also do not want centres to then say, "Oh, there is a new Bill; so, no choice, we have to increase fees." Just a message to everyone, the new Bill should not lead to fee increases.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Generally, the main cost drivers for preschools are rental and teachers' salaries.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: And we have no plans to change our space- and teacher-per-child requirement as they are currently satisfactory.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is very important to take note of that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This, hopefully, is also for centres to take note that the main cost drivers are not changed under these requirements.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This space continues to evolve and we intend to strengthen it in many different ways not addressed under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: These approaches that we are taking would also help centres carry out their responsibilities effectively without unnecessarily incurring costs in a very significant way.      .

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.55 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.35 pm until 3.55 pm.
